summary: Iteration 11. Everything ran on the isolated QA stack only (127.0.0.1:8088/order, backend 8101, mongod 27018). The preview URL and port 27017 were not touched. BACKEND: adapted and re-ran the suites serially. test_iter10_qa_cancel.py 11/11 passed. It now asserts: in-process cancel gives 'dipulihkan_setelah_dibatalkan' (1a x4 and the 20k-audit scale test); the blocked 503 is exactly the generic message with no backup id; the backup id and the 'memulihkan otomatis'/'Pulihkan manual' detail appear only in /api/settings/cleanup/status (the hammer thread now also polls status); <backup>, files and files/resi are all 0700. test_iter8_qa_crash.py 10/10 passed: kill -9/restart recovery gives 'dipulihkan_setelah_restart' and the blocked 503 is generic. test_iter9_qa_delta.py 4/4 and test_iter7_qa_regression.py 8/8 passed. NEW test_iter11_qa_bgfail.py 1/1 passed. It makes recover_journal really raise outside restore_and_verify by adding a Mongo validator that rejects every security_logs insert, using cancel:order_payments. Result: the wrapper caught the error ('Pemulihan latar gagal' logged), the journal went to needs_manual with problems=['pemulihan latar error: ...'], and STATE.blocked switched to the 'Pulihkan manual' message with the backup id (not stuck on 'memulihkan'). The reseller write got the generic 503, the data was already restored (diff empty), and CLI restore plus restart unblocked. The validator was removed afterwards. UI (Playwright, QA build, whose CleanupTab and MaintenanceBanner match /app src): (1) cancel:order_payments from the UI: the dialog closed, the preview reset, and the toast read 'Proses pembersihan terputus. Sistem memulihkan data otomatis; ...'. History right after the error still showed the old entry; after about 4s it showed 'Terhenti, dipulihkan otomatis & terverifikasi'. Snapshot diff empty, no journal. (2) FAIL_AFTER=orders: the toast showed the full 'dikembalikan otomatis dari backup dan terverifikasi ... Backup: cleanup-...' detail, the dialog closed, and history showed 'Gagal, data dipulihkan & terverifikasi'. Snapshot diff empty. (3) Blocked (cancel + FAIL_RESTORE, category orders): the reseller profile save showed only the generic maintenance toast, with no 'cleanup-' text anywhere on the reseller page; the DB address was unchanged. The super admin dashboard banner showed the manual message and 'Backup: cleanup-...'. Afterwards CLI restore and a normal restart. (4) Quick regression: admin2, reseller and super admin logins work; admin2 sees 'not allowed' on cleanup; reseller order detail renders the item, payment and shipment pagers (only checked that they exist; deep paging was not re-tested this round); the branding tab is visible (save was not re-tested); a normal UI cleanup of audit gave 'Berhasil' plus a success toast. End state: QA backend running with no CLEANUP_TEST_* vars, no cleanup_lock journal, health ok.

minor.issue: block() embeds the raw exception text untruncated. A pymongo WriteError produced a very long admin banner message containing the full errInfo/schema dump. problems[] is cut to 300 chars, but the STATE.blocked message is not. Truncate it (e.g. str(e)[:150]) or use a short generic reason. Admin-only, so the impact is cosmetic.

When the wrapper path is taken, no security_logs/history entry is written (for example 'gagal_pemulihan_otomatis'), so the Catatan Keamanan list shows nothing for this event. That is unavoidable when security_logs itself is failing, but for other exceptions a best-effort _security_log inside its own try would help.

Hammer writes that raced the cancelled request sometimes got 502 (nginx 'recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)'), seen in 2 of 4 1a runs. This is a side effect of asyncio cancellation of the request task closing the keep-alive upstream connection. Low impact: the test hook only, or a real disconnect.

integration_issues.issue: Every status >=500, including 503, takes the 'Proses pembersihan terputus. Sistem memulihkan data otomatis' branch. A 503 on execute (for example cleanup active in another tab or session, or the system blocked) would show a misleading 'terputus/memulihkan' toast instead of the 503 detail. Suggest only 500/502/504/no-response there, and errMsg(e) for 503.

The immediate refetch runs before background recovery finishes, so the old history is shown. The 3s refetch catches it for small data. If recovery takes longer than 3s (large data), history and status stay stale until a manual reload. Consider polling cleanup-status until blocked==null, then refetching history.

action_items: Optional: truncate the exception text in the _spawn_recovery fallback block() message.
Optional: in CleanupTab, treat 503 on execute with errMsg(e) rather than the 'terputus' toast.
Optional: poll cleanup-status after a cancel until blocked clears, then refetch history.
critical_code_review_comments: Delta (a) verified: cleanup.py:201-203 mkdir per level with 0o700; on disk <backup>, files and files/resi are 700.

Delta (b) verified by a real fault injection (security_logs validator): the wrapper sets needs_manual and blocks with the manual message. If even the _set_state/find_one fails, block() still runs with backup None ('-') and STATE never stays 'memulihkan'.
Delta (c) verified: source='cancel' gives dipulihkan_setelah_dibatalkan; startup gives dipulihkan_setelah_restart; the label is present in RESULT_LABEL.

Delta (d) verified: the middleware returns the generic 503 for every role while blocked; the active-cleanup 503 is unchanged ('Sistem sedang melakukan pembersihan data...'); the detail and backup id are only in /settings/cleanup/status (reseller gets 403 there, admin2 can read it).

Delta (e) verified in the UI: the dialog closes, the preview resets, the toast is correct for both the plain-text 500 (cancel) and the JSON 500 (verified rollback), and history and status are refetched immediately and again at 3s. Selected categories stay checked after a failure, which is fine.
